alignments.note: Rule 35: the ASV fuses preposition and relative into the portmanteau whereunto, whose -unto carries eis and where- the relative, so the pair is one aligned unit headed on the pronominal. Rule 45 does not apply, since part of the English answers to each token.
Rule 65: the particle is realized by also.
Finite verb with its English subject.
Two-word English preposition headed on the prepositional word.
Rule 20: his from autou occupies the determiner slot.
Rule 31: the article governs an expressed head noun and a participle follows, so which is the participle's helper and this second attributive article realizes nothing.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite clause, headed on the lexical verb.

Rule 94: the ASV renders the prepositional phrase by the single word mightily, so the pair is one unit, and rule 39's test keeps it aligned because might- answers to dynamei. Rule 34's pleonastic reading is not available here: dynamis alone glosses power, not mightily, so the adverbial force is the preposition's.

review_notes: The two compound units here are decided on opposite sides of the same test: whereunto spells both tokens and mightily spells one, and both stay aligned under rules 35 and 39 rather than noncompositional.
The marginal alternative (in power) does not change the pairing.
